name: Alpex Solar Ltd
tagline: Solar module maker backward-integrating into cells ahead of a DCR policy tailwind, tempered by rising leverage and a capacity-disclosure dispute
business_overview: Alpex Solar -- North India's largest solar PV module manufacturer (Greater Noida), backward-integrating into cell manufacturing (TOPCon) ahead of a mandated domestic-content policy shift.
fundamentals_table: D/E rising -- 0.96x per Q4 FY26 forum discussion (vs ~7% reported by some screeners; forum figure likely more current)
89% annual CAGR; Q4FY26 sales +105.3% YoY to Rs 671.96 Cr; FY26 revenue/profit nearly tripled
fundamentals_narrative: Exceptional headline growth and returns, but the forum discussion reveals D/E has risen materially (to ~0.96x) as the company funds a large capex program -- a more current and concerning figure than the low D/E some screeners report.
technical_read: Not pulled -- fundamentals and community due-diligence were the primary signal.
sentiment_summary: Read all 19 posts in the thread (2025-08 to 2026-08). Central catalyst: a Jun 2026 government policy requiring EPC players to use India-made solar modules with India-made cells (DCR), targeting the ~50GW of India's module capacity that currently imports Chinese cells. Alpex is building a 2.2GW TOPCon cell facility to capture this. Management has consistently delivered on guided doubling of revenue since IPO.
community_signal: No trusted users posted in this thread, but the non-trusted community debate is unusually well-informed and adversarial in a useful way: vikas_chandrawat (invested, 1.5yr holder) flagged receivables growing faster than revenue and rising interest costs as balance-sheet stress; a live, unresolved dispute in the most recent posts (Aug 2026) over whether the new cell facility's confirmed environmental clearance covers 1.6GW or the company-claimed 2.2GW -- a real execution-credibility question not yet settled.
bull_case: Specific, quantified DCR policy catalyst (Jun 2026) directly targets the exact gap Alpex is filling via backward integration into cell manufacturing
Consistent execution track record -- management has delivered on guided revenue-doubling every year since IPO
bear_case: D/E has risen to ~0.96x with tripling interest costs as the company funds its cell-capacity buildout -- balance sheet stress is real and current, not hypothetical

Live, unresolved dispute over whether environmental clearance actually covers the full claimed 2.2GW cell capacity or only 1.6GW -- a credibility/execution-timeline risk flagged by a well-informed community member, not yet resolved by management
verdict_headline: A specific, well-timed policy catalyst with genuine execution risk still being actively litigated by the community
verdict_reasoning: The DCR policy catalyst and backward-integration strategy are specific and credible, and management's delivery track record is real

Conviction held to Medium given the material rise in leverage and the unresolved environmental-clearance capacity dispute -- both current, unresolved, well-documented risks rather than resolved concerns
notes_short: DCR policy tailwind + cell backward integration, but D/E risen to ~0.96x and live EC-capacity (1.6GW vs claimed 2.2GW) dispute unresolved

four_box.note: DCR policy catalyst (Jun-2026) + backward integration into cell manufacturing is a real structural tailwind; no explicit market-cap/headroom or valuation data recorded; moat unclear beyond capacity fill; D/E risen to ~0.96x and disputed environmental-clearance capacity (1.6GW vs claimed 2.2GW) are separate execution risks.
